chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Durust al-Wasiti, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The dissimulation (taqiyya) of any one of you has not reached the dissimulation of the Companions of the Cave. Indeed, they used to attend the festivals and tighten the sashes, so Allah gave them their reward twice.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الْكَهْفِ: The Companions of the Cave (As'hab al-Kahf)
key_terms.الزَّنَانِير: The sashes (worn by Christians to distinguish themselves)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Companions of the Cave's practice of Taqiyya according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the Companions of the Cave as the ultimate exemplars of *taqiyya*, noting that their outward conformity—attending festivals and wearing distinctive sashes—was so profound that Allah rewarded them doubly. This hadith underscores the Shia principle that sincere internal faith, preserved through strategic external adaptation during periods of persecution, is highly valued and can yield multiplied spiritual rewards.
